data.ideal_summary: We performed ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and matched RNA-seq on human or mouse cells treated with an mTOR inhibitor (Torin1, rapamycin or INK128/sapanisertib) versus vehicle-treated controls. Ribosome-protected fragments and total mRNA were sequenced in parallel to calculate translation efficiency. Comparing treated and untreated samples identifies mRNAs, such as 5' TOP and TOP-like transcripts, whose translation is altered by mTOR inhibition.
method_notes: Translation efficiency requires matched Ribo-seq and RNA-seq from the same samples; Ribo-seq-only series cannot give TE changes.
Ribo-seq measures ribosome occupancy, not protein output; proteomics (e.g. pulsed SILAC) can confirm synthesis changes.
Rapamycin and Torin1/INK128 differ in effect on 4E-BP phosphorylation, so TE changes are inhibitor-dependent.
